title: Uncomplicated cellulitis on day 12 of antibiotics after clinical resolution

provenance.author: Claude Code (draft for owner review), case list approved by the owner

story: A 47-year-old woman admitted with nonpurulent cellulitis of the lower leg received IV cefazolin for 2 days, then oral cephalexin. On day 12 of antibiotics the erythema and warmth have resolved and she is afebrile; cephalexin has no stop date.

problems.title: Cellulitis of the left lower leg

results.text: Leukocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count

expected_findings.summary: Day 12 of antibiotics for uncomplicated cellulitis that has resolved; the recommended course is about 5 days, longer only without improvement.

reference_answer: Stop cephalexin: the infection has resolved and she has completed well over the recommended course.
rationale: For uncomplicated cellulitis IDSA recommends 5 days, extended only if the infection has not improved. She is already on oral therapy, so the IV to PO module must stay silent.

citations.supports: Duration of 5 days for uncomplicated cellulitis, extended if not improved.
Prospective audit and feedback of antibiotic therapy as a stewardship intervention.
